one_liner: Pure-Rust embeddable FLAC encoder library and CLI; its multithreaded mode outruns single-threaded flac 1.4.3 at near -8 compression.
what_it_does: A library that turns interleaved i32 PCM into a FLAC stream: you pass a `Source` (MemSource or your own implementation) and a TOML-serializable `config::Encoder` to `encode_with_fixed_block_size`, which returns an in-memory `Stream` of inspectable (serde-serializable) frames, subframes and residuals that you then write through a `BitSink`. It is not an API drop-in for libFLAC's stream encoder; the companion `flacenc-bin` CLI takes 8/16/24-bit WAV in and writes FLAC, configured by a TOML file rather than flac's -0..-8 presets. An experimental nom-based decoder sits behind the `decode` feature.
how_it_is_fast: It runs the standard FLAC search (constant, fixed and LPC subframes; left-side, right-side and mid-side stereo; partitioned Rice parameter choice) with a deliberately light default: LPC order 10 from one Tukey(0.4)-windowed autocorrelation and a Levinson recursion in f64, 15-bit coefficient quantization, and fixed-predictor order picked by an approximate-entropy estimate over 32 partitions instead of trial encoding. flac -8 searches more (max LPC order 12 with subdivide_tukey(3) windows). The windowed autocorrelation, residual computation and Rice bit-count table are written against std::simd (portable_simd); on stable a scalar `fakesimd` shim stands in, which is why the stable single-thread build is about 2.6x slower (126.5x vs 331.5x real time, derived from page data). In `par` mode the main thread reads and deinterleaves blocks into a pool of frame buffers, N worker threads encode frames independently over crossbeam channels, a separate thread updates MD5, and the frames are reassembled in order.
when_to_use: A Rust program that must emit FLAC without linking the C libFLAC: pure Rust, Apache-2.0, default dependencies are small (crc, md-5, heapless, crossbeam-channel).

Batch encoding of long recordings on a multi-core machine where wall-clock throughput matters: the 8-thread default measured 1309.5x real time vs 229.7x for single-threaded flac 1.4.3 -8 on a 4-core/8-thread Cascade Lake VM (nightly build).

Codec research or tuning: you want to inspect or post-process frames, subframes and residuals, change LPC order, window or stereo modes through a TOML config, or try direct-MSE LPC (`experimental` feature).
A nightly toolchain is acceptable: with `simd-nightly` one thread is 1.44x the speed of flac -8 at files about 0.4% larger (derived from page data).
when_not_to_use: Stable Rust only: the single-thread build runs at 0.55x of flac -8 and 0.22x of flac -5 (126.5x vs 230.9x and 572.1x real time), and the 8-thread default only ties single-threaded flac -5 (575.3x vs 572.1x), derived from page data.

You want the best ratio or a like-for-like multithreaded comparison: there are no -0..-8 levels, the default ratio (0.5276) sits between flac -8 (0.5256) and -5 (0.5328), block size is fixed, and flac 1.5.0 (February 2025) added multithreaded encoding in libFLAC and the flac CLI, which the reports do not test; an HN result snippet (thread not opened) cites flac -j16 at 5.47x its single-thread speed on 8 cores/16 threads.

24-bit material with abrupt noise-to-silence transitions: open issue #256 (flacenc 0.5.1) reports a 4096-sample 24-bit mono block encoding to about 3.08 GB instead of about 12 KB and overflowing STREAMINFO's 24-bit max_frame_size so decoders reject the file, and open PR #259 describes a u32 lane wrap in the Rice bit-count table at 24-bit signal-to-silence transitions; neither fix is merged.
Streaming or low-memory encoding: `encode_with_fixed_block_size` returns the whole encoded `Stream` and the CLI writes the file only after encoding finishes; a streaming API is still open issue #91.
32-bit PCM (open issue #226) or non-WAV input to the CLI.

integration.form: crate (`flacenc` on crates.io) plus the `flacenc-bin` CLI crate
integration.dependencies: crc, heapless, md-5, num-traits, rustversion, seq-macro; optional crossbeam-channel (`par`, default on), log and serde (default on), nom (`decode`), nalgebra (`experimental`), mimalloc
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.83 (MSRV, scalar fake SIMD); the `simd-nightly` feature needs nightly portable_simd, and crates.io 0.5.1 with it no longer builds on current nightly (issue #260; fixed on unreleased main by #249)
integration.platforms: any Rust target (portable code, no hand-written intrinsics; SIMD through std::simd on nightly); benchmarked only on x86-64 (Cascade Lake, AVX-512)
integration.thread_safety: In `par` mode the encoder spawns its own worker threads (default count = available_parallelism, settable through `workers` or an environment variable) plus an MD5 thread; thread safety of the public types is not documented.

gotchas: The crates.io release 0.5.1 (2025-12-18) lags main: it lacks RICE2 5-bit Rice parameters (#248; issue #246 saw a 24-bit step signal grow to 544 MB vs 47 KB at 16 bits), the portable_simd LaneCount fix (#249), and the STREAMINFO fix for inputs whose length is not a multiple of the block size (#255, merged 2026-06-29; strict decoders such as Symphonia rejected those files). The benchmark reports were built from unreleased main in May 2026, not from the published crate.

The measured binaries use target-cpu=native from the repository's .cargo/config.toml (AVX-512 on the test VM) plus fat LTO, codegen-units 1, panic=abort and mimalloc; set RUSTFLAGS and the release profile yourself to reproduce that build in your own project.
`mt1` (multithread with workers = 1) is not a one-core number: the reader/main thread and a separate MD5 thread run alongside the single worker. Only `st` (multithread = false) is single-threaded.

The flacenc-bin README warns that the encoder "very rarely outputs broken signals" and suggests checking with the reference decoder's MD5; the parallel path also hits an `unreachable!` panic on out-of-range input samples (open issue #224) instead of returning an error.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against rusty_flac (pure Rust, measured single-core against FFmpeg 8.1.2's native flac encoder rather than libFLAC) and go-flac (Go, slower than libFLAC in its own table), pick flacenc-rs for a Rust library with serializable frame components, configurable search and built-in multithreading that has been on crates.io since 2022 (about 703k downloads). HALAC compresses and runs faster but is not FLAC, and libfoxenflac only decodes.
verified_claims_summary: The repository's own report (pytools/reporter.py: one wall-clock CLI run per file and setting on four Wikimedia recordings, start-up and file I/O included, on a GCP c2-standard-8 Xeon Cascade Lake VM, 4 cores/8 threads) gives nightly flacenc 331.5x real time single-threaded and 1309.5x with 8 workers against flac 1.4.3 (generic ./configure build, single-threaded) at 229.7x for -8 and 550.4x for -5, with output 0.4% larger than -8; the stable build reaches 126.5x and 575.3x. Every flacenc output was decoded with flac -d and matched the input byte for byte, so the numbers are for lossless streams, but no configuration is both faster and at least as small as a tested flac setting at equal thread count.
status_note: Active but slow to release (last commit 2026-06-29; crates.io 0.5.1 from December 2025 misses several correctness fixes on main, and issues #256 and #260 show no maintainer reply); Apache-2.0 and copyable, but pin a main-branch commit if you need the RICE2 and STREAMINFO fixes.
